A1.justification: Both PDFs describe StateSpaceDiffuser. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching across revisions and relocations.

before.justification: v1 reports original MiniGrid experiments, backbone and state-feature ablations, CSGO generations and a 12-participant user study.

after.justification: v3 retains those empirical results and adds longer-context evaluations, recurrent-backbone comparisons, robustness tests and evaluation-seed statistics.

M1.justification: The Cosmos-tokenized Mamba branch, DIAMOND diffusion branch, feature/action fusion and staged training remain. v3 explicitly documents freezing the pretrained context branch and explains training stability; this does not establish a changed algorithm relative to v1's existing two-stage procedure.

E1.justification: MiniGrid Simple, MiniGrid and CSGO remain the evaluated environments. v3 adds lower- and higher-complexity MiniGrid variants and corrupted-input scenarios (Appendices B.5–B.6), extending environmental conditions within the existing navigation domain.

E2.justification: v3 adds LSTM and GRU to the MiniGrid memory-backbone comparison at context length 50 (Table 4). DIAMOND, State-Space World Model and S4 remain; the original S4-versus-Mamba comparison moves from v1 Table 2 to v3 Table 5 unchanged.

E3.justification: New protocols include training at context 50 and testing at 100/150 without finetuning, Gaussian noise on 11 middle frames with separate branch controls, and compute-adjusted scoring. Appendix A also changes the stated MiniGrid context-branch input from 144×144 to 32×32. This is a reported setting revision, without evidence that the retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v3 substantially expands analysis of context extrapolation, alternative recurrent backbones, computational cost, noise recovery and transfer across maze complexity (Table 2; Appendices B.1–B.6). The original zero-state ablations, S4 comparison and CSGO failure examples are retained or relocated, rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: Appendix B.4 newly reports four evaluation seeds at MiniGrid contexts 16 and 100, with means and standard deviations, including 41.00 ± 0.008 average PSNR at context 16. v1 has no corresponding seed-based summary. This documents evaluation variability, not four independently trained models.

E6.justification: Table 1 scores and CSGO preference ratings of 0.20/0.24 remain unchanged. v3 adds substantial results: at contexts 100/150, average PSNR is 37.99/30.75 versus DIAMOND's 26.39/24.35 (Table 2), alongside recurrent-backbone, noise, complexity, compute-adjusted and seed-summary results. These are additional evaluations, not improvements under the original unchanged settings.

T1.justification: Appendix B.1 introduces a limited mathematical scoring definition: multiplying existing scores by 1−0.006 or 1−0.018 to account for computational overhead. The state-space recurrence and prediction equations remain unchanged, and no new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The central contribution of combining persistent state-space memory with diffusion remains. v3 makes generalization beyond the training horizon an explicit contribution, quantifies context-branch overhead as below 2%, and revises the headline MiniGrid gain from 8.9 dB to 51.9% PSNR improvement.

C2.justification: v3 adds a substantive explanation of joint-training instability and why freezing the context branch helps (Section 4.2). Section 5.3 and the appendices expand discussion of noise recovery, complexity-dependent generalization, decoder quality and state-capacity bottlenecks. Appendix D.1 also explicitly qualifies CSGO context-50 performance as having substantially weaker memory.

D1.justification: v3 adds a project-page link and clarifies branch freezing, reversed CSGO action encodings, maze-generation parameters, recurrent-comparator interfaces and user-study participant provenance. Most hardware, optimization and training-budget information was already present. The revised 32×32 MiniGrid input remains unreconciled with the retained 1296-dimensional feature specification.

R1.justification: v3 adds discussion and citations for Pandora, Long Context Tuning, visual representations and perceptual evaluation. Appendix B.2 identifies S4WM as the closest prior model and explains using an S4-backbone comparison as a proxy. The established positioning around summarizing the entire history remains.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work and methodology receive extensive paragraph-level rewriting and expanded explanations. v3 adds a main-text strengths/limitations section and reorganizes previously dispersed analyses into a dedicated StateSpaceDiffuser Properties appendix, substantially changing the narrative structure.

P2.justification: v3 adds five quantitative tables covering new evaluations and analyses, redraws Figure 2 and expands explanatory captions. It splits v1's CSGO ablation Figure 18 between main-text Figure 8 and appendix Figure 9, relocates existing tables and panels, and revises MiniGrid comparison-row labels in v1 Figure 10/v3 Figure 12.

improvement.justification: The additional recurrent baselines, longer-horizon and robustness tests, evaluation-seed statistics and clearer training explanations strengthen the existing empirical case. The central method and main results were already established in v1, so the gain is primarily better validation and documentation. Reproducibility remains imperfect: v3 introduces an unresolved input-resolution discrepancy, while the retained claim of a 9.1 PSNR advantage over S4 still disagrees with Table 5's 27.09 versus 24.29.
